text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy on Friday blamed a halt in growth in its international traffic and higher costs for a sharp fall in first-half 1996 profits.
Finnair forecast clearly lower full-year earnings.
Finnair said pre-tax profit fell almost 50 percent to 233.5 million markka ($50.8 million) in the first half from 463 million in the year-ago period.
Net sales inched ahead to 3.67 billion markka from 3.62 billion last year but operating costs rose to 3.23 billion markka from 2.97 billion in 1995.
The median of analysts' forecasts for the state-controlled airline had been for a 292 million markka profit in a 152 million to 372 million range.
"On the basis of the performance trend of the first half of the financial year, it ... can be expected that the full-year operating result will be clearly below last year's," Finnair said.
Finnair's operating profit was 624 million markka in the last financial year to March 31, 1996.
Aircraft fuel costs rose some 20 percent on average over the period, adding 60 million markka to costs in the first half.
Finnair said earlier this week it was raising air fares to help offset higher fuel costs.

Finnair said there had been an about-face in the Finnish air market, as growth in international scheduled flights came almost to a standstill although domestic traffic and chartered flights picked up clearly.
"A recovery is ... expected in international traffic at the end of the year, although the situation remains unstable," Finnair said.
Finnair plans structural measures to boost its profitability.

"We at Finnair have set the goal of achieving structural changes ... so that the group's ability to make profits will improve by a yearly level of about 500 million markka by the start of the next millenium," Finnair chief executive Antti Potila said.
"We can't afford to wait... because costs outstrip revenue. Action must be taken," Potila said. "We have to strike a balance between income and expenditure."
